In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leading order result is not a reliable one.
the neutrino emissivity in the presence of the weak neutral vector interactions is enhanced up to O(v_F^2) compared to the standard Fermi liquid theory.

the neutrino emissivity in the presence of a neutral vector interaction is enhanced compared to that of the standard weak interaction, and that the enhancement is more significant for lower values of the Fermi velocity, which is characteristic to the baryons in the inner regions of compact stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutrino emissivity from weak neutral vector interactions is enhanced by a factor of 2-4 for v_F< 1/3 compared to the leading-order result.
the weak neutral vector current is not suppressed in the low energy regime, contrary to what is expected by the naive dimensional analysis.
the neutrino emission rate in compact stars is enhanced compared to leading order by about 20%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leading order result for neutrino emissivity should not be used in the study of cooling of compact stars.
neutrino emissivity of compact stars can be enhanced by a few percents by including vertex corrections.

the leading order result in the Fermi liquid theory for the neutrino emission rates is not a good approximation for the neutrino emissivity of baryonic matter at finite temperature and densities relevant for the compact stars.
